title: Command-Line (CLI) and Programmatic R Workflow
text: Run Rscript run_query_optimizer.R --help display supported command-line flags:
code: Usage: Rscript run_query_optimizer.R --bib <file.bib> [options]  Options:   --bib <path>           Path to BibTeX input file (required)   --out <dir>            Output directory (default: output)   --config <path>        Optional YAML configuration file   --min-recall <num>     Minimum seed recall 0..1 (default: 0.60)   --max-hits <num>       Maximum PubMed hits cap (default: 2000; Inf for no cap)   --max-evals <int>      Maximum live query evaluations (default: 60)   --max-gs-chars <int>   Max Google Scholar query characters (default: 256)   --custom-query <str>   Custom PubMed query to evaluate (repeatable)   --custom-label <str>   Optional label for next/last --custom-query   --no-cache             Disable disk API response caching   --email <str>          Email for NCBI polite pool   --ncbi-key <str>       NCBI API key (or set NCBI_API_KEY env var)   --help, -h             Show this help message and exit

what: Benchmarking Your Own Manual Query Against the Pareto Frontier
title: Command-Line (CLI) and Programmatic R Workflow
text: Use --custom-label --custom-query (repeatable) evaluate one manual queries alongside automatically discovered Pareto frontier:
code: Rscript run_query_optimizer.R \   --bib path/to/seed_articles.bib \   --min-recall 0.90 \   --max-hits 1000 \   --custom-label "Manuscript query" \   --custom-query '((H5N1[Title/Abstract] OR H5[Title/Abstract]) AND (Influenza[Title/Abstract]) AND (fatal*[Title/Abstract])) NOT (H7N9[Title/Abstract] OR H1N1[Title/Abstract] OR H1N1pdm09[Title/Abstract])' \   --out output_benchmark

what: Using an NCBI API Key for Faster Execution
title: Command-Line (CLI) and Programmatic R Workflow
text: default, NCBI E-utilities allows ~3 requests per second. Setting NCBI_API_KEY (NCBI_EMAIL) increases rate limit ~10 requests per second:
code: export NCBI_EMAIL="researcher@university.edu" export NCBI_API_KEY="your_ncbi_api_key_here"  Rscript run_query_optimizer.R \   --bib path/to/seed_articles.bib \   --out output

title: Command-Line (CLI) and Programmatic R Workflow
text: reproducible pipelines, can store term overrides, custom concept blocks, benchmark queries YAML file pass --config config.yml (config_path = "config.yml" R):
code: # Maximum Google Scholar query character limit (hard ceiling: 256) max_gs_chars: 256  # Maximum number of AND-connected concept blocks (1..4) max_blocks: 3  # Maximum OR-synonyms per concept block max_terms_per_block: 5  # Terms that MUST appear in the primary concept block required_terms:   - h5n1  # Candidate terms to ignore during automatic extraction banned_terms:   - world health organization   - united states  # Exclusion terms applied via PubMed NOT (...) and Google Scholar -term / -"phrase" # Supports prefix wildcards (*) and title:-scoped exclusions (-intitle: in Google Scholar) exclude_terms:   - h7n9   - h1n1*   - vaccin*   - title:ferret*  # Optional manual concept blocks (leave empty/commented for automatic PICO discovery) # custom_blocks: #   pathogen: #     - h5n1 #     - h5 #   outcome_severity: #     - fatal* #     - mortality #     - death* #   population_host: #     - cases #     - human*  # Optional custom PubMed queries to benchmark alongside the Pareto frontier custom_queries:   - label: "Manuscript query"     pubmed_query: '((H5N1[Title/Abstract] OR H5[Title/Abstract]) AND (Influenza[Title/Abstract]) AND (fatal*[Title/Abstract])) NOT (H7N9[Title/Abstract] OR H1N1[Title/Abstract] OR H1N1pdm09[Title/Abstract])'

code: library(revlitquery)  res <- optimize_search_queries(   bib_path   = "path/to/seed_articles.bib",   output_dir = "output",   min_recall = 0.90,   max_hits   = 1000,   max_evals  = 60,   custom_queries = list(     list(       label = "Manuscript query",       pubmed_query = paste0(         "((H5N1[Title/Abstract] OR H5[Title/Abstract]) AND ",         "(Influenza[Title/Abstract]) AND (fatal*[Title/Abstract])) ",         "NOT (H7N9[Title/Abstract] OR H1N1[Title/Abstract] OR H1N1pdm09[Title/Abstract])"       )     )   ) )  # Inspect the Pareto-optimal query table res$pareto_df[, c("rank", "combined_recall", "pm_hits", "gs_chars", "pubmed_query", "google_scholar_query")]  # Inspect concept-grouped exclusion hints head(res$exclusion_hints, 10)

title: Command-Line (CLI) and Programmatic R Workflow
text: can also call stage revlitquery pipeline individually. self-contained offline demonstration using small synthetic BibTeX corpus:
code:
library(revlitquery)  # 1. Write and parse a 6-article demo BibTeX file demo_bib <- file.path(tempdir(), "demo_seeds.bib") revlitquery:::.write_demo_bibtex(demo_bib) #> [1] "/tmp/RtmpPDMTLG/demo_seeds.bib"  seeds_df <- parse_bibtex(demo_bib) seeds_df[, c("citekey", "year", "pmid", "title")] #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   citekey                   year  pmid     title                                 #>   <chr>                     <chr> <chr>    <chr>                                 #> 1 li2008estimates           2008  18439345 Estimates of the case fatality rate … #> 2 wang2012serological       2012  22362880 Serological evidence of human infect… #> 3 fiebig2011epidemiological 2011  21679679 Epidemiological and clinical charact… #> 4 kandun2008factors         2008  18959499 Factors associated with case fatalit… #> 5 lai2016global             2016  27211899 Global epidemiology of avian influen… #> 6 cowling2013comparative    2013  23803488 Comparative epidemiology of human in… # 2. Prepare local seed text fields (offline; use enrich_seeds() for live PubMed enrichment) seeds_local <- seeds_df seeds_local$in_pubmed <- nzchar(seeds_local$pmid) seeds_local$full_title <- seeds_local$title seeds_local$full_abstract <- seeds_local$abstract seeds_local$full_text <- tolower(paste(seeds_local$title, seeds_local$abstract))  # 3. Extract candidate n-grams and prefix wildcards (offline mode: probe_pubmed = FALSE) terms_df <- extract_candidate_terms(   seeds_df     = seeds_local,   config       = list(),   probe_pubmed = FALSE ) #> Warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: `all_keywords`. #> Warning: Unknown or uninitialised column: `mesh_terms`. head(terms_df[, c("term", "n_words", "df_tiab", "df_title", "lift", "term_score")], 10) #> # A tibble: 10 × 6 #>    term               n_words df_tiab df_title  lift term_score #>    <chr>                <int>   <int>    <int> <dbl>      <dbl> #>  1 avian influenza          2       5        5 1267.       4.01 #>  2 human h5n1               2       5        2 1267.       3.90 #>  3 h5n1                     1       6        6  190.       3.54 #>  4 case fatality            2       5        2 1267.       3.39 #>  5 human                    1       6        5  190.       2.94 #>  6 influenza                1       6        5  190.       2.94 #>  7 case fatality rate       3       3        1 9495.       2.55 #>  8 fatality                 1       6        2  190.       2.54 #>  9 avian                    1       5        5  158.       2.47 #> 10 case                     1       5        3  158.       2.22 # 4. Discover PICO / semantic concept blocks blocks <- build_concept_blocks(   terms_df = terms_df,   seeds_df = seeds_local,   config   = list(max_blocks = 3, max_terms_per_block = 4) ) str(blocks) #> List of 3 #>  $ :List of 2 #>   ..$ name : chr "primary_topic" #>   ..$ terms: chr [1:2] "avian influenza" "influenza" #>  $ :List of 2 #>   ..$ name : chr "outcome_severity" #>   ..$ terms: chr [1:2] "case fatality" "fatality risk" #>   ..- attr(*, "narrow_term")= chr "case fatality rate" #>  $ :List of 2 #>   ..$ name : chr "population_host" #>   ..$ terms: chr [1:2] "human" "confirmed human" #>   ..- attr(*, "narrow_term")= chr "confirmed human" #>  - attr(*, "block1_coupled")= chr [1:4] "avian influenza" "h5n1" "influenza" "avian" #>  - attr(*, "joint_hits")= Named num(0)  #>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr(0)  #>  - attr(*, "term_families")= Named chr [1:45] "primary_topic" "primary_topic" "primary_topic" "outcome_severity" ... #>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:45] "avian influenza" "human h5n1" "h5n1" "case fatality" ... #>  - attr(*, "domain_qualifier")= chr "h5n1" # 5. Translate a structured query specification into PubMed & Google Scholar syntax q <- make_query(   blocks = list(     list(name = "primary_topic", terms = c("h5n1", "h5"), field = "tiab"),     list(name = "domain_context", terms = "influenza", field = "tiab"),     list(name = "outcome_severity", terms = c("fatal*", "case fatality"), field = "tiab")   ),   exclude_terms = c("h7n9", "h1n1*", "vaccin*") )  cat("PubMed query:
", to_pubmed_query(q), "

") #> PubMed query: #>  (("h5n1"[tiab] OR "h5"[tiab]) AND ("influenza"[tiab]) AND ("fatal*"[tiab])) NOT ("h7n9"[tiab] OR "h1n1*"[tiab] OR "vaccin*"[tiab]) cat("Google Scholar query:
", to_google_scholar_query(q), "
") #> Google Scholar query: #>  (h5n1 OR h5) influenza fatal -h7n9 -h1n1 -vaccine

title: Interactive Shiny Interface Guide
text: application opens (clicking Run Query Optimizer left sidebar), Pareto Explorer tab displays: 1. Seed Papers (BibTeX): Upload .bib file click Load sample H5N1 .bib. status pill shows number loaded entries many contain abstracts. 2. Sensitivity vs. Specificity: Adjust target Minimum seed recall (%) (e.g., 75% 90%), Max PubMed hits cap (default 2000, 1000 tighter specificity), Google Scholar char limit (<= 256). Moving recall slider changing hit cap dynamically updates recommended query plot threshold lines without re-querying PubMed. Top Value Boxes: Summarize total seed papers (many resolved PubMed abstracts), currently selected query’s seed recall (100.0%, 48 / 48 PubMed seeds), total PubMed hits (540, within <= 1,000 cap), Google Scholar character count (146 / 256). Red star: recommended Pareto-optimal query meeting minimum recall maximum hit cap. Blue circles: non-dominated Pareto frontier queries (Q1, Q2, …). Gray circles: Dominated candidate queries evaluated Stage 1 Stage 2 search. Clicking point plot (row Pareto table ) loads query Selected Query Inspector card. Selected Query Inspector Card: Displays side--side PubMed Query Google Scholar Query boxes one-click Copy buttons, Open PubMed / Open Google Scholar verification links, list missed seed citekeys. Figure 1: Pareto Explorer tab showing sensitivity-specificity Pareto frontier, summary value boxes, Selected Query Inspector card (100% seed recall 540 PubMed hits).

what: revlitquery: Reverse Literature Review Search Query Optimizer
title: revlitquery: Reverse Literature Review Search Query Optimizer
text: Given .bib file target/seed papers systematic literature review, revlitquery reverse-engineers semantically equivalent PubMed Google Scholar (<= 256 characters) boolean search queries optimizes sensitivity (seed recall) vs. specificity (total hit count) Pareto frontier using NCBI E-utilities: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities): live total hit counts, single-request seed PMID retrieval checks, year-assisted title resolution, per-PMID disk caching. Google Scholar: exact semantic translation adhering Google Scholar syntax (intitle:, implicit , uppercase , -exclude, <= 256 characters) clickable verification links. Concept-Grouped & Wildcard Exclusion Mining: stratified timeline sampling non-seed PubMed results synthesize prefix wildcards (vaccin*, cell*, mutat*, phylo*, reassort*, duck*, ferret*), classify exclusions scientific concepts (competing_subtypes, experimental_lab, vaccines_immunology, veterinary_ecology), build greedy set-cover exclusion blocks 0 seed loss.
